overview: DESeq2 analysis of 12 samples (6 control, 6 treated; organism assumed human, ~64% of gene IDs unannotated synthetic placeholders) identified 875 significant genes and, on preranked GSEA across Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways, a highly concordant signature: activation of NF-κB/interferon-γ/cytokine innate-immune programs paired with suppression of oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial electron transport — the well-established fingerprint of innate-immune activation, not a novel biological discovery. The top individual gene hits (IL15RA, PTGS2, CDKN2B) are largely explained by this same NF-κB/IFN axis and raise a secondary, testable hypothesis of a senescence-associated secretory phenotype, while a discordant NRF2/PRDX1 gene pair points to unresolved mitochondrial or electrophilic stress rather than adaptive antioxidant protection. Treatment identity, cell-composition origin of the signal, and the ~64% unannotated gene fraction all remain open and materially limit translational interpretation.
conclusions:
The dominant, most statistically robust result of this run is not any single gene but a pathway-level pattern replicated independently across three gene-set databases: NF-κB/TNFA signaling, interferon-γ response, cytokine and IL-1 family signaling, and cytosolic DNA sensing are all up in treated samples, while oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial electron transport are down. This is textbook innate-immune 'immunometabolic switch' biology — the transcriptional fingerprint of LPS/TLR-, TNF-, or IFN-γ-driven monocyte/macrophage activation documented from foundational mouse work through human sepsis and autoimmune-tissue transcriptomics. Its concordant appearance across Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways corroborates that the enrichment call is real rather than a database-specific artifact, but the pattern itself is confirmatory of known biology, not novel — the useful next question is which cell population and which stimulus produced it, not whether the pattern is real.

The top individually significant genes are consistent with, and mostly explained by, this same axis. IL15RA (the single largest fold-change in the entire dataset) and PTGS2 (COX-2) are both established, directly-mapped NF-κB and IFN/STAT1 target genes, so their induction is mechanistically unsurprising given the pathway signal — it corroborates rather than extends the enrichment finding. CDKN2B (p15INK4b), however, sits on a partially distinct TGF-β/SMAD-driven cell-cycle-arrest axis that is coupled to NF-κB-driven secretory output only through the CEBPB-dependent senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) program. Their co-occurrence is a coherent, literature-grounded hypothesis — the treatment may be inducing a senescence-like state with CDKN2B marking the arrest arm and IL15RA/PTGS2 the inflammatory secretory arm — but this is a hypothesis for this specific dataset, not an established result; confirming it would require examining additional canonical SASP markers (IL6, CXCL8, CDKN2A, CDKN1A) not singled out here.

A second, more genuinely unexpected observation runs against the grain of canonical pathway logic: NFE2L2 (NRF2) transcript is up, but its directly-cloned, canonical ARE target PRDX1 is down, while UQCRC2 (a mitochondrial Complex III subunit whose loss causes a bona fide human mitochondrial disease) is the single most downregulated named gene. The dominant literature model has NRF2 activation raising antioxidant targets concordantly and generally supporting, not suppressing, mitochondrial respiration — the observed discordance contradicts that model. The more parsimonious interpretation, grounded in oncometabolite/SDH-pathway literature, is that primary mitochondrial or electrophilic stress is the upstream driver of both the OXPHOS/ETC gene suppression and an NFE2L2 transcriptional rise that has not (in this dataset) achieved coordinate downstream antioxidant output — i.e., an unresolved stress response rather than successful adaptive protection.

Translational distance is short on interpretability and long on actionability. None of these findings can be tied to a specific drug or exposure because treatment identity is never stated in the inputs. Bulk RNA-seq cannot distinguish cell-intrinsic metabolic reprogramming from a shift in immune-cell composition/infiltration — both produce an identical NF-κB-up/OXPHOS-down bulk fingerprint, as shown directly in lupus-tissue precedent — so this run characterizes a pathway-level state, not a validated target or biomarker. The most concrete, if still hypothesis-level, translational read is a possible safety signal: if the treatment is genotoxic or otherwise senescence-inducing, the CDKN2B/SASP-like pattern and the mitochondrial-stress/NRF2-discordance pattern both merit follow-up as candidate toxicity signatures rather than as therapeutic opportunities.

findings.title: Convergent NF-κB/interferon-γ immune activation coupled to oxidative phosphorylation suppression across Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways
findings.description: Preranked GSEA independently run against three collections shows concordant, statistically strong enrichment: up in treated — Hallmark TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB (NES=2.99), INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE (NES=2.80), INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE (NES=2.12); Reactome Cytokine Signaling in Immune System (NES=2.22), Interleukin-1 family signaling (NES=2.33); WikiPathways Cytosolic DNA sensing pathway (NES=2.32). Down in treated — Hallmark OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION (NES=-3.05); Reactome Aerobic respiration and respiratory electron transport (NES=-2.59), Mitochondrial protein degradation (NES=-2.39); WikiPathways Electron transport chain OXPHOS system in mitochondria (NES=-2.82).
findings.literatureInterpretation: This bidirectional pattern (NF-κB/IFN-γ/cytokine signaling up, OXPHOS/ETC down) is one of the best-characterized transcriptional signatures in immunology — the LPS/TLR-driven glycolytic switch of monocyte/macrophage activation, reproduced from foundational mechanistic work through human sepsis and autoimmune-tissue bulk transcriptomics. Its concordance across three independently-annotated databases corroborates data quality rather than indicating novel biology. Bulk RNA-seq cannot distinguish intrinsic cellular reprogramming from a shift in immune-cell composition/infiltration, both of which produce this identical fingerprint.

references.relevance: Foundational demonstration that LPS drives macrophages toward glycolysis with concordant transcriptional suppression of mitochondrial/OXPHOS genes via succinate-HIF-1α.
Shows succinate/SDH-driven mitochondrial ROS repurposes mitochondria from ATP synthesis toward inflammatory signaling in activated macrophages, mechanistically linking the two arms of the pattern.
Human sepsis patients show the same OXPHOS-to-glycolysis transcriptional/metabolic shift as the signature of acute innate immune activation, with IFN-γ reversing the defect in immunoparalysis.
Human monocyte bulk transcriptomic GSEA reporting the near-identical combined pattern: TNF/TLR/JAK-STAT/interferon signaling up with ~120-170 OXPHOS/mitochondrial genes down.

Human lupus tissue shows the same bulk-level co-occurrence attributable largely to inflammatory/myeloid cell infiltration rather than intrinsic reprogramming — key caveat for interpreting bulk (non-single-cell) data.

findings.title: Top DE genes (IL15RA, PTGS2, CDKN2B) suggest a possible senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-like program
findings.description: IL15RA is the single largest fold-change hit in the entire dataset (shrunken log2FC=6.45, padj=3.9e-49); PTGS2/COX-2 is strongly upregulated (log2FC=2.96, padj=3.3e-13); CDKN2B/p15INK4b is also strongly upregulated (log2FC=2.91, padj=5.6e-26). IL15RA and PTGS2 are established, directly-mapped NF-κB and IFN/STAT1 target genes consistent with the pathway-level signal; CDKN2B is a TGF-β/SMAD-driven cell-cycle-arrest effector coupled to NF-κB-driven secretory output via the CEBPB-dependent SASP program.
findings.literatureInterpretation: IL15RA and PTGS2 induction are individually expected, well-established NF-κB/IFN-target responses that corroborate the pathway-level enrichment call rather than extend it. Their co-occurrence with CDKN2B — a marker from a distinct TGF-β/SMAD senescence axis linked to NF-κB-driven secretory genes only through the SASP program — is a biologically coherent but unverified hypothesis specific to this dataset, not an established finding; it has not been confirmed against other canonical SASP markers.

references.relevance: Maps a functional NF-κB site in the human IL15RA promoter, the mechanistic basis for NF-κB-driven IL15RA induction observed here.
Shows IFN treatment and IRF-4 activate the IL15RA promoter in human monocytes, explaining co-induction with the IFN-γ response enrichment.
Senescent tumor cells upregulate IL15/IL15RA as part of a senescence-associated NK-cell-engaging secretory program, direct precedent for the SASP hypothesis.
Establishes PTGS2/COX-2 as a canonical, near-obligatory NF-κB/inflammatory target gene.
TGF-β induces CDKN2B (p15INK4b)-dependent senescence independent of p53/p16, establishing CDKN2B's primary regulatory axis as distinct from direct NF-κB control.

findings.title: NRF2 (NFE2L2) upregulation is discordant with its canonical antioxidant target PRDX1, amid coordinated mitochondrial/OXPHOS gene suppression
findings.description: NFE2L2 (NRF2) transcript is significantly upregulated (log2FC=3.23, padj=1.0e-13) while PRDX1, its directly-cloned canonical ARE target gene, is significantly downregulated (log2FC=-2.91, padj=3.9e-15). UQCRC2, a structural mitochondrial Complex III subunit, is the single most downregulated named gene in the dataset (log2FC=-4.43, padj=2.3e-18), consistent with the pathway-level OXPHOS/electron-transport suppression seen across all three GSEA collections.
findings.literatureInterpretation: The literature's dominant model has NRF2 activation concordantly raising antioxidant targets like PRDX1 and generally supporting (not suppressing) mitochondrial respiration — the observed inverse pattern contradicts this canonical coupling. The more parsimonious, literature-grounded reading is that primary mitochondrial/electron-transport impairment and associated electrophilic or oncometabolite stress (e.g., SDH-pathway-type mechanisms) are the upstream driver of both the OXPHOS suppression and an NFE2L2 transcriptional rise that has not achieved coordinate downstream antioxidant output — an unresolved stress response, not adaptive protection.

references.relevance: Clones the human PRDX1 promoter and shows it is a direct, canonical NRF2/ARE target lost in Nrf2-knockout cells — establishes the expected concordant direction that this dataset's pattern contradicts.

Shows Nrf2 loss impairs and Nrf2 gain improves mitochondrial membrane potential/respiration — the dominant literature model is NRF2-supportive, not suppressive, of OXPHOS, contrary to the pattern observed here.

Demonstrates Complex II dysfunction and fumarate accumulation drive KEAP1-NRF2 activation, offering an alternative causal model in which mitochondrial impairment is upstream of the NRF2 transcriptional response.
Establishes UQCRC2 loss-of-function as a cause of human mitochondrial Complex III deficiency, confirming UQCRC2 as a genuine, disease-relevant OXPHOS structural gene anchoring this signature.

themes.name: NF-κB-driven innate immune activation, with a possible senescence-associated secretory component, dominates the treated-vs-control transcriptome

findings.title: Convergent NF-κB/interferon-γ immune activation coupled to oxidative phosphorylation suppression across Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways
Top DE genes (IL15RA, PTGS2, CDKN2B) suggest a possible senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-like program

themes.narrative: The strongest, most reproducible signal in this run is pathway-level NF-κB/IFN-γ/cytokine activation, independently confirmed across three gene-set databases. The individual top DE genes trace directly back to this axis: IL15RA and PTGS2 are established NF-κB/IFN-STAT1 targets that corroborate rather than add to the pathway call. CDKN2B, however, marks a distinct cell-cycle-arrest program that the SASP literature couples to NF-κB-driven secretory genes, raising a testable hypothesis that the treatment induces a senescence-like inflammatory state rather than generic immune stimulation alone. This remains a hypothesis, not a confirmed mechanism, for this specific dataset.

themes.name: Coordinated mitochondrial/OXPHOS suppression is accompanied by a non-protective, atypical NRF2 response, pointing to unresolved electrophilic or metabolic stress

findings.title: Convergent NF-κB/interferon-γ immune activation coupled to oxidative phosphorylation suppression across Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways
NRF2 (NFE2L2) upregulation is discordant with its canonical antioxidant target PRDX1, amid coordinated mitochondrial/OXPHOS gene suppression

themes.narrative: Pathway-level GSEA across all three databases independently confirms coordinated suppression of oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial electron transport; at the gene level this is anchored by UQCRC2, a genuine Complex III subunit whose loss causes human mitochondrial disease. Concurrently, NFE2L2 (NRF2) transcript rises while its canonical antioxidant target PRDX1 falls — a pattern that contradicts the literature's dominant model of concordant NRF2-driven antioxidant and mitochondrial support. The most parsimonious reading is that primary mitochondrial or electrophilic/oncometabolite stress is driving both an incomplete NRF2 response and genuine ETC gene suppression, rather than NRF2 activation itself causing the mitochondrial phenotype.

limitations: Treatment/perturbation identity is never stated in metadata; all biological interpretation of the NF-κB/OXPHOS signature and the SASP/NRF2 hypotheses is necessarily generic (consistent with LPS/TLR exposure, sepsis-like inflammation, cytokine exposure, or a genotoxic/senescence-inducing agent) rather than mechanism-specific to a known intervention.

Bulk RNA-seq cannot distinguish cell-intrinsic metabolic/inflammatory reprogramming from a shift in immune-cell (myeloid) composition or infiltration — both produce an identical NF-κB-up/OXPHOS-down bulk signature per documented precedent in lupus tissue; no cell-type deconvolution was performed in this run.

Organism was assumed human throughout (annotation database, all three GSEA gene-set collections) with no organism field in the raw inputs to confirm this; if the true organism differs, every finding in this synthesis, all of which depend on human-specific annotation, would be invalid.

63.8% of tested gene IDs are synthetic placeholders with no real biological identity; every finding here is drawn only from the ~36% of genes carrying real annotation, and per-set gene-set coverage for some significant Reactome/WikiPathways hits was as low as ~35-45% of nominal membership, so statistical significance for those sets may not reflect the true, fully-annotated pathway.

The SASP hypothesis (IL15RA/PTGS2/CDKN2B) and the NRF2/PRDX1 discordance are both post hoc interpretive hypotheses grounded in mechanism-level literature, not validated in this run against additional marker genes (IL6, CXCL8, CDKN2A, NQO1, HMOX1) or at the protein/functional level.

Only one GSEA ranking metric (signed Wald statistic) was used and the shallow sample (sample_01) was retained based on a QC judgment call without a with/without sensitivity re-analysis at the modeling stage; both were pre-specified but unreplicated methodological choices that could shift specific gene/pathway rankings.

keyReferences.description: Foundational mechanistic paper establishing the LPS-induced macrophage glycolytic switch with concordant OXPHOS gene suppression — the core precedent for this run's dominant pathway-level pattern.
Human sepsis patient data directly demonstrating the OXPHOS-to-glycolysis transcriptional/metabolic shift as the in vivo signature of acute innate immune activation.
Human monocyte bulk transcriptomic GSEA reporting a near-identical combined TNF/IFN-up, OXPHOS-down pattern — the closest direct analog to this run's GSEA result.

Human lupus tissue bulk expression data showing the same NF-κB-up/OXPHOS-down co-occurrence is attributable to immune-cell infiltration — key caveat for interpreting this run's bulk (non-single-cell) data.
Maps the functional NF-κB site driving IL15RA induction, the mechanistic basis for this run's single largest fold-change hit.
Establishes precedent for senescent cells upregulating IL15/IL15RA as part of a SASP-like secretory program, grounding this run's SASP hypothesis.
Defines the TGF-β/SMAD-driven CDKN2B senescence axis, distinct from direct NF-κB control, central to interpreting CDKN2B's role in the possible SASP signature.
Establishes PRDX1 as a direct, canonical NRF2/ARE target gene — the reference model against which this run's NRF2-up/PRDX1-down discordance is judged atypical.
Shows NRF2 canonically supports rather than suppresses mitochondrial respiration, the literature baseline this run's mitochondrial-stress interpretation departs from.
Confirms UQCRC2 as a genuine human mitochondrial Complex III disease gene, validating the gene-level anchor of the OXPHOS-suppression signature.
